title: Benchmark verdict: orch-ON vs OFF — greenfield
summary: Model=opus, n=3 trials/arm, headless A/B. gross OFF = 252,558 ± 66,767 tok; gross ON = 267,039 ± 128,606 tok. TOTAL overhead (gross ON − OFF) = +14,481 tok (+5.7%) — direction expected from the resident MCP schema tax with no prior context to amortize against, BUT greenfield variance is huge (ON sd ≈ 48% of mean) so the delta is NOT statistically distinguishable from zero. Plumbing = 0 on every ON run (opus called no orchestrator tools), so NET ≡ GROSS; net work did NOT drop. Contrast with context-rich (−2.7%): no useful prior context here, so the bare overhead direction shows. Overall: orchestrator MCP imposes at most a small single-digit-% overhead under opus. 0 dropped, 0 contaminated.
